name: blazeblogger
why: A tiny shell-script blog CMS from the old school, a curious relic if you like seeing how far plain text goes.

brief.what_it_is: BlazeBlogger is a command-line content management system for building static websites and weblogs. According to its homepage, it is a simple-to-use but capable CMS for the command line that produces static content without database servers or server-side scripting, and it suits anything from a personal weblog to a project page or company site. The homepage does not spell out inputs and outputs in detail; the brew entry lists nine executables (blaze, blaze-add, blaze-config, blaze-edit, blaze-init, blaze-list, blaze-log, blaze-make, blaze-remove), which suggests a set of subcommands that manage entries and generate the site. The homepage describes RSS feed generation, HTML and XHTML output, and a configurable markup processor (core.processor).
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a way to run a website from the command line with no database and no server-side scripting, which keeps the output as plain static files.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says it produces static content without database servers or server-side scripting. The 1.0.0 release note says a core.processor configuration option lets the user choose whatever markup language they want. Beyond that, I did not see the mechanism explained.

commands_seen.context: Gentoo install command from the 2010 Gentoo package announcement; the post says to switch to superuser and run it at a shell prompt.

brief.install_notes: Packages exist for Gentoo (emerge blazeblogger, as superuser), Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu Lucid Lynx, Arch Linux (AUR, stable and development versions), and Slackware (a SlackBuild archive hosted at slackwarium.org.uk, with a SlackBuild Usage HOWTO). Nothing on the homepage covers setup beyond package installation. The brew formula's caveats are empty.
brief.standout: It is a shell-script blog CMS that generates static sites with no database, and its own user guide and bash completion point to a deliberately old-school, text-first workflow. The homepage also lists a 'Support Us' request asking users to add themselves to the Ohloh users list.
brief.status: Quiet. The most recent release on the homepage is 1.2.0 on 2011-02-20, and the newest post is a Slackware packaging note from 2011-05-05. The homepage shows nothing newer. I did not find a commit history or repository, so I cannot confirm more.
brief.caveats: The docs site (docs.blackened.cz) requires JavaScript and cookies, and the fetch returned only a notice with a link to a static table of contents, which I did not follow, so command details are thin. Support is via an IRC channel (#blazeblogger on freenode) and a discussion group. The homepage is an old static blog and may be out of date.
quotes: BlazeBlogger is a simple-to-use but capable CMS for the command line that produces static content without the need of database servers or server side scripting.

BlazeBlogger 1.0.0 has been finally released! The most significant change from the latest release is probably the addition of core.processor configuration option making it possible to use whatever markup language user wishes, as well as introduction of bash completion and quick reference card.
If you have any questions, comments, requests, or you just want to chat with me and/or other BlazeBlogger users, feel free to join #blazeblogger on freenode.
fetch_log: http://blaze.blackened.cz/ — worked; returned the blog-style homepage with release history and About text.
http://docs.blackened.cz/ — loaded but only returned a notice that JavaScript and cookies are required, with a link to a static table of contents that I did not follow.
